summary: 68-year-old man with a hard, painless, eccentric left subareolar lump with nipple retraction for 2 months; sister had breast cancer. NICE NG12: men ≥50 with a unilateral firm subareolar mass → suspected cancer pathway; mammography/ultrasound and core biopsy.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Hard lump behind the left nipple
inputs.hpi: Painless hard lump behind the left nipple for 2 months; the nipple has started to turn in. Sister had breast cancer at 55. No medications. No weight loss.

exam.other: Left breast: 2 cm hard, irregular, eccentric (upper outer to the nipple) mass tethered to the areola with nipple retraction; firm left axillary node. Right breast normal. Testes normal.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Suspicious left male breast mass — exclude carcinoma
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Suspicious breast mass (left) in a 68-year-old man: hard, eccentric, nipple retraction, axillary node, family history. Suspected cancer pathway: mammography and ultrasound, core biopsy; consider BRCA2 testing.

mustNotMiss.note: Unilateral hard eccentric subareolar mass with nipple retraction in a man ≥50.

guideline.name: NICE NG12 — Suspected cancer: recognition and referral
guideline.section: Site-specific recommendations: breast cancer (age ≥30 unexplained lump; ≥50 unilateral nipple discharge/retraction; skin changes; men ≥50 subareolar mass), haematological cancers (unexplained lymphadenopathy), head and neck (unexplained thyroid lump)
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Suspected cancer: recognition and referral. NICE guideline NG12. London: NICE; 2015 (updated).

guideline.name: Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms (ABS / RCR, Department of Health)
guideline.section: Triple assessment (clinical examination, age-appropriate imaging, needle biopsy); imaging by age; nipple discharge; breast infection; breast pain
guideline.citation: Willett AM, Michell MJ, Lee MJR (eds). Best practice diagnostic guidelines for patients presenting with breast symptoms. London: Department of Health / Association of Breast Surgery; 2010.

rationale: Permutation: sex and features. Same demographic (older man) as the gynaecomastia base but unilateral, hard, eccentric, retracted nipple. Tests that the male-breast pathway does not default to gynaecomastia.
